2. Though these petitions were heard and disposed of by separate judgments by a Division Bench of the High Court Division, the law points involved in all these petitions being similar, these petitions are disposed of analogously by this order. 

 3. Civil Petition No. 602 of 2003 arose out of Writ Petition No. 3536 of 2010, Civil Petition No. 603 of 2011 arose Out of Writ Petition No. 3559 of 2010, Civil Petition No. 673 of 2011 arose of Writ Petition No. 3532 of 2010, Civil Petition No. 679 of 2011 arose out of Writ Petition No. 3531 of 2010, Civil Petition No. 649 of 2011 arose out of Writ Petition No. 4456 of 2010 and Civil Petition No. 1830 of 2011 arose Out of Writ Petition No. 4455 of 2010. The High Court Division in all these petitions directed the writ respondents to absorb the petitioners (writ petitioners) in revenue budget, upon satisfaction that the latter can satisfy the criteria laid down in clause 4 of the rule contained in the Gazette cited above or they can bring themselves within the purview of the ECNEC resolution or that those, whose jobs were previously regularized on "pick and chose" basis do not stand on different footing. 

 4. We have perused the writ petitions, the judgments of the High Court Divisions and heard the learned counsel of both the parties at length. Mr. Mahbubey Alam, learned Attorney General appearing for the petitioners by taking us to the averments in the writ petitions argued that the Case of each writ petitioners is quite distinguishable, as such, the High Court Division erred in law in making all the rules absolute without application of its judicial mind. Learned Attorney General further argued that some of the writ petitioners had no locus stanch to maintain a petition in the nature of mandamus but the High Court Division gave all the writ petitioners reliefs without arriving at specific findings as to their entitlement to the relief asked for in the petitions. Learned Attorney General further argued that the High Court Divisions failed to appreciate the ratio in the cases of Bangladesh Vs. Shaft Uddin Ahmed, 50 DLR (AD) 27 and Ashatush Chakma Vs. Rajuk, 60 DLR 273 and some other decisions of Indian jurisdiction and illegally followed the said cases which are quite distinguishable. 

 5. Learned Attorney General added that the executive Committee of the National Economic Council (ECNEC) by its decision dated 10th January, 2008 formulated the guide lines for transfer of the officers and employees working in different development projects to the revenue budget after completion of the respective projects but the High Court Divisions though noticed the same, committed fundamental error in directing the writ respondents to absorb the writ petitioners in the revenue set up without giving any finding on whether the petitioners satisfied the criteria formulated by it on the facts averred in the petitions. There is no finding, it is submitted, whether or not the projects in which the writ petitioners are working have been completed when they have moved the High Court Division for judicial review of the impugned notifications. Learned Attorney General Finally submitted that the High Court Division failed to take into consideration that after completion of a project under the development budget, the entire menpower of that project would be transferred to revenue budget if any person working in any particular project intends to he absorbed in the revenue budget subject to the availability of a vacant post and in such case also, such employee will not be entitled to any relaxation as regards his age and qualification. 

 6. Mr. Rokanuddin Mahmud, learned counsel on the other hand, contended that the High Court Divisions in fact did not give the writ-petitioners full reliefs in the light of their prayers made in the writ petitions, rather it directed the writ respondents to consider the case of the writ petitioners after being satisfied that the criteria laid down in clause 4 of the Gazette dated 20th June, 2005 and the decision of the ECNEC and then to absorb the writ petitioners in the revenue budget whose jobs were previously regularized. It is further contended that the point in issue involved in the petitions has already been resolved by this Division in unreported cases in Civil Petition Nos. 767, 796, 1084, 1085 and 1091 of 2011, therefore, the High Court Division has committed no error of law in giving the above directions. 

 8. In this petition 109 persons challenged the notification under memo dated 16th March, 2010 published for recruitment of 95 computer operators against the vacant posts in the revenue budget in the Local Government Engineering Development (LGED). In the cause title the writ petitioner Nos. 13 Gul Nahar and 38 Kolpona Rani Sarkar did not mention their present status in the projects in which they, are working. Petitioner No. 50 Hafez Ahmed mentioned that he has been working as Lab technician, the petitioner No. 104 Hosneara Begum stated that she has been working as socio economist. Other writ petitioners mentioned that they are working as computer operators in different projects. They mentioned the dates of their joining in different projects and stated that they are still working in different projects. The cases of writ petitioner Nos. 13, 38, 50,104 are quite distinguishable. 

 9. In this petition 196 persons challenged the notification under memo dated 16th March, 2010 issued by the writ respondent No. 3 for recruitment of 581 Work Assistants against the vacant posts in the revenue budget in LGED. In this petition all the writ petitioners other than the writ petitioner No. 67 Saiful Islam, No. 119 Md. Mukhlesur Rahman, and No. 190 Gazi Mesbabour Rahman did not mention in the cause title that they are working as Work. Assistants. They are working as lab technicians and Lab Assistants. The cases of the above three writ petitioners are quite distinguishable. In paragraph 24 of the writ petition, they stated that they "are serving in various projects of the Local Government Engineering Department (LGED) under the Ministry of Local Government, Rural Development and Co-operatives....... Therefore, admittedly all these writ petitioners are also, working in different projects and the projects are yet to be completed on the day of filing of the writ petition. 

 10. In this petition there are 83 petitioners, who challenged the Notification dated 16th March, 2010 issued by the writ respondent No. 3 for recruitment of 90 Office Assistants in the vacant posts in revenue budget in the LGED. All the petitioners in the cause title other than the writ petitioner No. 2 Nazma Sultana, the writ petitioner No. 11 Md. Anisur Rahman, the petitioner No. 12 Farhana Sultana, the petitioner No. 13 Shamsad Begum, the petitioner No. 16 Md. Mostafizur Rahman, the petitioner No. 54 Mrs. Sarifa Akter and the petitioner No. 77 Roma Rani Saha did not mention their status, the petitioner No. 6 Nilam Nahar who mentioned that she has been working as monitoring assistant, the petitioner No. 9, Md. Morshed Alam who mentioned his status as UDA. RRMAIDP, the petitioner No. 19 Md. Shafiur Rahman and the petitioner No. 49 Md. Saiful Islam who mentioned that they are working as community organizers, the petitioner No. 57 Md. Abdus Samad who mentioned that he is working as community organizer and the petitioner No. 76 Runa Zinnat mentioned that she is working as monitoring officer, are claiming to have been working as Office Assistants. In paragraph 13 all the petitioners admitted that they are "serving in various projects of the Local Government Engineering Department (LGED)........." 

 12. There are 200 petitioners who sought for a direction in the nature of mandamus to regularize their service under revenue budget in the LGED. In the petition they stated that they were appointed as drivers under different projects. They stated that the writ respondents published an advertisement in the Daily Ittefaq on 13th October, 2006 for recruitment of drivers, MLSS and other posts, that some of the writ petitioners applied for the posts of driver and appeared in the written examination but they were not recruited. They also claimed in paragraph 9 that they are serving as drivers in different projects of LGED and that the authority did not regularize their service in the revenue budget despite assurances given in that regard. 

 13. In this petition 112 persons sought for a direction for regularizing their service in the revenue budget. The entire in are claiming to have been working in different projects as MLSS. It is stated that on 13th October, 2006 LGED published an advertisement for 15 MLSS posts but the writ petitioners were not appointed. In paragraph 15 they stated that they are Still Serving in various projects of LGED. on perusal of cause title of the writ petitions, noticed that the writ petitioner No. 22 Md. Moshur Rahman and No. 27 Md. Abdul Latif mentioned their status as guards, the writ petitioner No. 28 Md. Jasim Uddin, a lift operator, the petitioner No. 45 Md. Mesbabur Rahman, a messenger, the petitioner No. 69 Md. Salim and the petitioner No. 70 Md. Abdul Mannan as guards, the petitioner No. 92 Idris Ali, a photo copy operator; the petitioner No. 93 Md. Sahob Uddin, a lab operator, the petitioner No. 96 Md. Aminur Rahman did not mention his status and writ petitioner No. 100 Md. Mostala Bepari, a photo copy operator. 

 14. In all the petitions the writ petitioners stated that they prayed for absorbing in the revenue set up but their prayers were unheeded to despite assurances given by the authority. The High Court Division noticed the Rules framed by the Government for regularizing the service in the revenue budget in respect of those officers and employees who are working in the development projects and to determine their seniority by Gazette Notification dated 28th June, 2005 and the decision of the ECNEC dated 10th June, 2008, and observed that the rules and the decision of ECNEC are sheet anchor for resolving the issues involved in the petitions. The learned Judges after quoting Rule 4 of the Rules of 2005 and the decision of the ECNEC dated 10th January, 2008 observed that though the decision of the ECNEC is not a law Within the meaning of Article 152 of the Constitution, nonetheless the writ petitioners, on the concept of legitimate expectation can claim as of right to be absorbed in revenue budget. 

 15. The Rules of 2005 were frothed in exercise of powers under Article 133 in conformity with Article 140(2) of the Constitution for regularizing the service of those who have been working in the development projects and for deciding their seniority. Sub-rule (1) of Rule 4 said, subject to the conditions provided in Clauses-(Ka), (Kha), (GA), an officer Or an employee can be regularized subject to the condition that such officer or employee was appointed after fulfillment Of the requirements necessary for the purpose of appointment as an officer or employee in the Government service, that there Must be continuity in service, and that before regularization in the revenue budget, if such officer or employee's :service are found satisfactory. 

 16. ECNEC being the executive committee of the Government in Making decision on economic policy, even if. it is assumed that, a decision made by the ECNEC has no force of law but by the same time, as per practice being followed by the Government, it cannot implement any project which has financial ,involvement without its approval. In its meeting under reference, it was clearly decided সমাপ্ত প্রকল্পের জনবল বিদ্যমান বিধিবিধান অনুসরনপূর্বক রাজস্ব বাজেটে স্থানান্তরের ব্যবস্থা করতে হবে। that is, the employees who are under the development projects can be transferred in the revenue budget only after completion of the those projects and that's too, after following. The formalities This decision of the can, not be ignored in view of the fact that it is the highest policy making body in implementing a decision of the Government which requires financial involvement, It is to be noted that as per policy of the Government, over which the Court normally does not interfere, an officer or an employee of an ongoing project cannot claim as of right to be transferred absorbed in the revenue budget for obvious reason for, if he is absorbed in the revenue budget such incomplete project will likely he affected for shortage of efficient staffs. It is only those employees whose projects were completed could claim as per decision of the ECNEC and the rules of 2005 to be transferred in the revenue budget. 

 17. The High Court Division did not make any finding as to whether on the facts pleaded in the writ petitions, the writ petitioners fulfilled the above criteria for absorption in the revenue budget against the posts advertised by the writ respondent No. 3. As huge number of posts in the LGED are lying vacant since March, 2010, though we find some inconsistency in the, impugned judgments, we feel that these matters should not he dragged any further for the interest of justice. The High Court Division directed the writ respondents to absorb the writ petitioners in the revenue budget after considering each of the writ petitioners case, if they fulfill the criteria laid down in the rules of 2005 or as per decision of the ECNEC. This operating part of the judgment is not clear, rather confusing which requires to be modified for removing doubts in considering the cases of the writ petitioners in the light of ECNEC's decision and the Rules of 2005. Accordingly, we dispose of these matters with the modification of the directions given by the High Court Division as under: 

 (1) An employee or an officer of Any development project can claim for regularization in the revenue set up if the project in which he is working is completed. 

 (2) Such officer or employee must have been appointed after following the recognized procedures being followed by the Government in appointing Government servants. 

 (3) Such officer or employee must have requisite qualification for the post he is seeking absorption: 

 (4) Such officer or employee must have continuity in service in the project in which he is working. 

 (5) Such officer or employee must have satisfactory service record before regularization the revenue budget. 

 (6) If an officer and employee whose rank and status did not relate to the posts advertised by the impugned Notifications on the day of its publications, such officer or employee will not be eligible for consideration for absorption. 

 18. The writ respondents shall follow the above guide lines for absorbing the writ petitioners in the revenue budget.
